clue.text: Source of food in buffet, say

definitions.note: a root vegetable is a source of food

indicators.note: say signals that the word for buffet is to be spoken, and a soundalike written

parts.note: to buffet is to strike repeatedly, to beat

explanation.surface: Pointing to where the food comes from at a buffet spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a meal, but here it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant grown for its edible root (and for sugar) is a food source.

clue.text: One travelling group of rugby players welcomed by supporter

indicators.note: welcomed by puts the rugby group inside the supporter

parts.note: a backer supports someone
the pack is a rugby team's forwards

explanation.surface: A travelling rugby squad greeted by a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One travelling' is the definition, not part of the rugby scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget traveller carrying belongings in a rucksack is someone travelling.

clue.text: Summary chapter from long story book

indicators.note: from says the chapter letter comes away from the long story

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A summary of one chapter of a long story book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes C away from EPIC, leaving EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: Its older meaning is an abstract or digest, a condensed version of a work.

clue.text: Porcelain top hat

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head or of a hat
a derby is a bowler hat

explanation.surface: An item of china shaped like a top hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown Derby is a famous English porcelain made in Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is a long-established make of English fine china, so the name stands for the porcelain itself.

clue.text: Game included in novel title or noted work

indicators.note: included in places the game inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters of title or are made anew

parts.note: Go is a board game

explanation.surface: A game embedded in a novel's title or another famous work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is the anagram signal on TITLE OR, and 'noted' is a pun: a work full of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera is a famous musical work, 'noted' hinting at notes.

clue.text: Vibrating sound used to be on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as broadcast, heard rather than seen

parts.note: were is a past form of to be

explanation.surface: A vibrating noise that used to be heard on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech, without a sounded R, 'were' and this word sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuous buzzing or humming noise, as of wings or machinery spinning.

clue.text: Shot in past of Europe struggling with tragedy?

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A historic photo of Europe struggling with a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges EUROPE and TRAGEDY together; 'Shot' is a photograph, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: An early photograph made on a silvered plate, a shot from the past.

clue.text: Money invested with a North African chap

indicators.note: invested means put inside, so the letter for with goes into the money

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Cash put into a business with a North African man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition: the man is from central Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the central African republic of that name is an African chap.

clue.text: Bostonian's name featuring in gossip?

indicators.note: featuring in says the name letter appears inside the gossip

parts.note: to yak is to chatter

explanation.surface: A Boston resident's name cropping up in tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Bostonian as an example: a New Englander.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for an American, originally a New Englander such as a Boston native.

clue.text: Wife in the country close to catching rabbit

indicators.note: the wife's letter sits in the middle of the country's name

parts.note: China is the country

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here of catching

explanation.surface: A wife abroad nearly catching a rabbit for the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is not the animal: in British slang (from rhyming 'rabbit and pork', talk) to rabbit is to chatter, and a rabbit is a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British colloquial words for a long, idle chat or gossip session.

clue.text: I go round with casino employee — an intriguing sort

parts.note: one who goes round, turning or wheeling, is a wheeler
the card dealer works at a casino table

explanation.surface: Someone circling with a croupier, a schemer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I go round' is read as a self-description: something that wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrewd operator who schemes and does deals, an intriguer.

clue.text: Drive home during cloudburst after midnight

indicators.note: after places the shower's word following the letter from midnight

parts.note: during means in
the middle letter of the word night
a cloudburst is heavy rain

explanation.surface: Driving home late at night through a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive home' is not a journey but a phrase meaning to fix an idea firmly; 'midnight' gives the middle of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a lesson home is to instil it deeply, which is what fixing a habit firmly in someone means.

clue.text: Computer nerd placing screw by nut

indicators.note: by means placed beside, next in line

parts.note: a ship's screw is its propeller
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A techie fixing a screw beside a nut in some hardware job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screw' and 'nut' look like hardware; they are a ship's propeller and the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an obsessive technology enthusiast, from the beanie hat with a spinner on top.

clue.text: Reverse order with great excitement

indicators.note: great excitement stirs up the letters of order and great

explanation.surface: An order to reverse given with great enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse order' looks like a single phrase; 'Reverse' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving backward or going back to an earlier state is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Basket case's beginning to feel very giddy

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of case's

parts.note: to reel is to feel dizzy and unsteady

explanation.surface: A basket case starting to feel dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basket case' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Basket'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker basket used by anglers for carrying fish.

clue.text: Patience goalie, oddly, doesn't show in a daze

indicators.note: in places the goalie's remaining letters inside the daze word

parts.note: a daze is a trance

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of goalie are not shown, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A dazed goalkeeper fails to turn up, testing everyone's patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly, doesn't show' looks like part of the football story, but it tells you to drop the odd-numbered letters and keep the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the capacity to put up with things, the forbearance this word names.

clue.text: Help to wind up a husband in a state

indicators.note: in places the wound-up husband pieces inside the state

parts.note: a land is a nation or state
to wind up is to end

explanation.surface: Assisting someone to rile their husband into a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' looks like tease; it means end.
explanation.definitionFit: Offering assistance is the idiom for helping someone.

clue.text: I wondered about what keeps retired people warm

indicators.note: about signals the letters of I wondered are moved around

explanation.surface: Musing on what pensioners use to stay warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests pensioners, but here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt stuffed with duck feathers keeps those who have gone to bed warm.

clue.text: Meetings holding up live discussions

parts.note: to be is to live, exist

explanation.definitionFit: Formal arguments or exchanges of views are discussions.

clue.text: Objective of person yelling, not quiet

explanation.definitionFit: Objective in the sense of external to the mind, outside, rather than subjective.

clue.text: See one wearing suit that's not worth mentioning

parts.note: a lawsuit is a trial

explanation.surface: Noticing someone in a suit, nothing worth remarking on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something petty and insignificant is not worth mentioning.

clue.text: Year's ban light, maybe, after such police activity?

parts.note: the letters of Year's, with its S

clue.text: Do summer job, little one at university

clue.text: Sticks up for superior

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: gums are sticks, glues

explanation.surface: Standing up for a superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks up for' reads as defends, but 'Sticks' is the verb glues.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior in the sense of self-satisfied and complacent.

clue.text: Rating a China set

clue.text: Country mile bounded by a heath

clue.text: Possibly slugs back a party drink by sink

by in the sense of beside: the sinking piece is set right next to the drink

parts.note: a do is a party
port is a fortified wine
to sag is to sink

explanation.definitionFit: Slugs and snails are examples of molluscs in this zoological class, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Navy spend recklessly, it's said

definitions.meaning: navy is a dark shade of the colour
